messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <skhan@acme.ai>

Subject: Monthly dashboard: latency/cost/uptime anomalies & QBR owner asks

Hi all,

Attaching the November dashboard (monthly_dashboard_Nov2026.pdf) and a short runbook draft for the QBR (qbr_runbook_draft_v2.docx). Two things jumped out from the platform report:

- Latency: 95p latency increased by ~18% the week of Nov 9. The spike is concentrated in the multi-tenant hosted pool serving short-chat workloads.
- Cost: Token spend per session rose ~12% MoM; idx shows higher small-batch tail usage and increased lossless decoding costs.
- Uptime: One minor regional failover on Nov 11 that resulted in a 7-minute window of degraded API responses.
- Usage: ACME's traffic shifted 30% to longer contexts after their new feature launch, which correlates with the latency bump.

Samira, looping you so the account team has the signal — the customer noticed a slowdown in their nightly processing window and flagged us. We should treat this as a QBR agenda item.

Asks / proposed owners (please confirm by EOD Mon):
- Investigate 95p spike root cause and mitigation plan: vivek_kulkarni
- Cost opportunity analysis (small-batch policy + quantization profile suggestions): laura_bennett
- Draft QBR slide + runbook excerpt focusing on mitigation and timeline: tessa_morgan
- Account sync & customer context: Samira Khan / Acme AI

I put a preliminary note in SUP-3892 (link below).

Thanks — please reply inline with any changes.

--
Jordan Blake
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <skhan@acme.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI finance <acct_team@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Monthly dashboard: latency/cost/uptime anomalies & QBR owner asks

Jordan, thanks for the quick heads-up and for attaching the dashboard.

To add customer color: we shipped a multi-turn analytics feature on Nov 8 which increases average context length and the number of parallel sessions during our nightly window. We saw the degradation at ~02:15 local time on Nov 12 and it surfaced as timeouts in 0.8% of jobs (these were retried by our app and completed).

The customer would appreciate: 1) a short explanation of root cause and a timeline for fix, and 2) any temporary mitigation (e.g., reduced concurrency cap) they can apply on their side while Redwood implements a server-side fix.

Happy to be on the QBR call and present the usage changes from ACME if that helps.

Samira
Senior PM, Integrations — Acme AI
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <skhan@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Monthly dashboard: latency/cost/uptime anomalies & QBR owner asks

Quick triage notes after a first-pass on the traces (see latency_spike_trace.json):

- Symptom: increased tail latency on short-chat endpoints; KV cache miss rate increased ~3x for those workloads during the spike windows.
- Probable cause: eviction contention after a small cache-size change rolled out to the shared pool on Nov 7 (we pushed a tuning patch to decrease memory footprint). That reduced cache effectiveness for bursty short requests.
- Short-term mitigations we can push in 48 hours: roll back the tuning for the affected pool (will increase memory but restore 95p latency), and apply a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap for ACME (config change).
- Longer-term: automatic cache-size autoscaling based on observed context-length distribution and a per-tenant cache partition to reduce noisy neighbor effects.

I'll draft a short playbook for Tessa to include in the runbook. Owner commitment: I can implement the rollback and per-tenant cap test by Dec 1 afternoon if leadership signs off.

Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <skhan@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Monthly dashboard: latency/cost/uptime anomalies & QBR owner asks

Thanks all — concise plan below for the QBR slide deck and leadership asks. I pulled a quick cost delta summary too.

Executive summary (to show in QBR):
- Impact: ~18% rise in 95p latency for short-chat endpoints for a 7-day window; 12% MoM token cost increase driven by small-batch tail and higher average context length from ACME.
- Root cause (probable): cache tuning rollback + customer usage pattern change (ACME feature).
- Customer impact: transient timeouts (0.8% jobs) — ACME retried and completed; they flagged customer support.

Action items + owners (finalized):
1) Immediate rollback to pre-Nov7 cache tuning on affected pool (Vivek) — ETA: 2026-12-01 COB.
2) Apply per-tenant concurrency cap for ACME as temporary mitigation (Vivek + Samira) — ETA: 2026-12-02 AM.
3) Cost/opportunity analysis: recommend small-batch policy + quant profile for ACME to reduce per-token spend (~5-8% potential) (Laura) — draft due 2026-12-03.
4) QBR slide + runbook excerpt: include timeline, customer ask, and post-mortem follow-ups (Tessa) — draft slides by 2026-12-02 EOD.
5) Leadership note & exec summary for QBR: Jordan to confirm and include in monthly leadership packet.

I'll prepare a one-page cost delta visual and a 3-bullet mitigation timeline for the deck. Jordan — please confirm that leadership is OK with the rollback and the short-term per-tenant cap.

Laura
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <skhan@acme.ai>

Leadership sign-off: approved to proceed with the rollback and per-tenant cap test. I'll include the executive summary in the leadership packet and confirm the QBR agenda with Sales. Tessa, please use the runbook excerpt in qbr_runbook_draft_v2.docx and add the playbook section Vivek mentioned.

- Samira to confirm whether ACME will accept a temporary concurrency cap, and provide preferred test window.
- Tessa to share draft slides by EOD 2026-12-02.

Thanks everyone — I’ll open a short 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the deck if needed.
